# Movement and space

## Movement, Speed, and Difficult Terrain
A creature may move up to its Speed on its turn, combine movement modes, and split movement around activity. Each foot in Difficult Terrain costs one extra foot, so it effectively consumes movement at half normal progress even when several causes overlap. On a grid, each square is five feet and an ordinary adjacent square costs one square of movement; a Difficult Terrain square costs two. Never assume a visually short route is open or reachable.

## Climbing, crawling, Prone, and standing
Without the matching special speed, climbing and swimming cost one extra foot per foot, and crawling costs one extra foot per foot; Difficult Terrain adds another extra foot. A creature can drop Prone on its turn without an action or movement if its Speed is not zero. While Prone, its only movement is crawling unless it stands; standing costs half its Speed for the turn and is impossible when Speed is zero.

## Creature size, space, and narrow passages
Tiny creatures share one five-foot square; Small and Medium occupy one; Large, Huge, and Gargantuan occupy two-by-two, three-by-three, and four-by-four squares. A creature's space is controlled fighting room, not its literal body. SRD movement permits passing through an ally, an Incapacitated creature, a Tiny creature, or one at least two sizes different, subject to occupancy rules; another creature's space can be Difficult Terrain. In SRD 5.2.1, a narrow opening sized for a creature one category smaller is Difficult Terrain; it has no separate legacy squeeze penalties.

The board rules engine represents footprints as one, four, nine, or sixteen occupied cells and requires an explicit narrow-opening region plus squeezed placement. It reduces the controlled footprint by one size for Small through Gargantuan, but the squeezed state alone does not add movement cost; the opening cells must also be authored as Difficult Terrain to apply the SRD cost. Use the visible footprint and terrain mark rather than assuming geometry.
